name: Lucas Lepri Knee Cut System
description: Study gi knee-cut passing with a focused Lucas Lepri course match, practical partner drills, clear decisions, and ways to review your progress.
summary: The Lucas Lepri Knee Cut System links knee-cut entries from open guards to adjustments for lasso grips, underhooks, and leg entanglements before establishing top control.
overview:
A familiar knee cut can feel different against each open guard because the entry grips and first obstruction change. Organize the practice around how you arrive at the cutting position and what stops you there. This makes a failed attempt easier to review than treating every guard as the same problem.

Precision Knee Cut Passes by Lucas Lepri is the matched instructional. Lepri covers entries from De La Riva and toreando movement, lasso responses, and adjustments against scoop grips and underhooks. The drills, sequence, and assessment criteria below are an original BJJGraph study plan; use them to organize practice alongside the course and feedback from a coach.
key_principles: Check the entry grips before trying to finish the knee cut.
Name the first obstruction instead of forcing the same movement.
Treat a lasso grip and an underhook as different problems.
Keep balance while changing the passing direction.
Evaluate the landing as part of the knee-cut attempt.

key_components.description: Choose one De La Riva or toreando entry and pause when the cutting position is reached to check what control you actually have.
key_components.purpose: Separate access to the position from the finishing movement.

key_components.description: Let the defender retain a specified lasso grip and work only on the reviewed grip-and-position response before attempting the cut.
key_components.purpose: Identify the obstruction created by the sleeve connection.

key_components.description: From a stalled knee cut, give the defender an underhook attempt and compare continuing the pass with changing direction.
key_components.purpose: Keep the upper-body exchange in the passing decision.

key_components.description: Continue the chosen cut until the leg clears, then ask the defender to recover a frame before resetting.
key_components.purpose: Complete the pass through the final control exchange.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The knee reaches the gap but the torso remains disconnected.
common_obstacles.solution: Pause at the entry and have a coach check the upper-body control.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The lasso grip redirects every attempt.
common_obstacles.solution: Begin with the lasso already set and isolate the relevant grip response.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The defender comes up on an underhook.
common_obstacles.solution: Add that response to a constrained round and rehearse an agreed branch.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A faster entry hides the same finishing problem.
common_obstacles.solution: Remove speed from the entry and test the final leg clearance separately.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: Choose one De La Riva or toreando entry and pause when the cutting position is reached to check what control you actually have. Then connect it to lasso obstruction. Compare the first lost control point after each round. Keep the first repetitions cooperative and agree on resistance, space, and reset conditions. Once the starting task is clear, add one defensive option at a time and compare the result with the intended control objective.

flashcards.question: What should you examine when the same knee cut fails against different guards?
flashcards.answer: Identify the entry grips and first obstruction in each guard instead of assuming the finishing movement is the only problem.

flashcards.question: Why isolate the open-guard entry from the finish?
flashcards.answer: Pausing at the cutting position reveals whether useful control exists before you commit to clearing the leg.

flashcards.question: How should a lasso-specific practice round begin?
flashcards.answer: Start with the agreed lasso grip established and work on the reviewed response before adding the full knee cut.

flashcards.question: What does an underhook change during a knee-cut attempt?
flashcards.answer: It changes the upper-body contest and may require a different response rather than continuing the original passing direction.

flashcards.question: What is the final objective of a knee-cut repetition?
flashcards.answer: Clear the trapped leg and establish a defined top position while accounting for the defender's immediate recovery.

flashcards.question: Why begin with familiar entries rather than jumping variations?
flashcards.answer: A familiar entry lets you observe grip and control problems without adding movement demands that obscure the diagnosis.
